Strokes I can actually see: a mahpakh-shaped '<' under the shin of אֲשֶׁר and again under הַבּוֹחֵר; a pashta-type stroke above the final letter of בָּחַר and of בַּתּוֹרָה; zaqef dots above טוֹבִים, הָעוֹלָם, עַבְדּוֹ and עַמּוֹ; a stroke above the resh of both בָּרוּךְ; a stroke above the tav of the second אַתָּה; sublinear accents under וְרָצָה, בְדִבְרֵיהֶם, הַנֶּאֱמָרִים, בֶּאֱמֶת (where independent-174 also notes accent strokes hard to separate from meteg), וּבְמֹשֶׁה, וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל, וּבִנְבִיאֵי and הָאֱמֶת; and a silluq stroke under the tsade of וָצֶדֶק. Independent-174 says the same: 'it carries accent-like marks (te'amim) as well as vowels. Those marks are not transcribed.' I found no human adjudication that drops them.
issues.required: Do a human or high-resolution accent pass and encode the printed te'amim, and meteg where distinct. At my resolution I can't name every sign with certainty, so I am not supplying a reading.
